text:
maya: FYI nightly harness flagged a candidate kernel for weird tail latency on long seqs.
perf-bot: Nightly sweep 3345127890: candidate kernel 'archwise_v2' — perf delta: +15% p50, +48% p99 for seq>=2048 on Ampere. artifacts attached.
liam: ugh, that's the kernel that changed prefetch stride in PR #8123
nora: do we have repro commands from the harness?
sam: yes: ```./bench --model=redwood-small --kernel=archwise_v2 --device=ampere --seq-len=4096 --batch=1 --iters=300 --kv-mode=prefix``` reproduces the spike
alex: I ran it locally, also saw KV cache thrash logs: "kv_cache_evictions: 1.02x" and GB/s drop in mem_bandwidth
maya: where does batching come in? this kernel also altered the continuous-batching path right? 
liam: it changed the stride which interacts badly with KV layout when seq grows, plus batching heuristics coalesce requests differently for long prefix reuse
nora: quick summary from perf traces: more L2 misses during kv lookup, higher stall cycles when seq>2048. flamegraph: https://perf.internal/reports/3345127890/archwise_v2
perf-bot: attached microbench artifacts: s3://redwood-ci/archwise_v2/3345127890/
sam: CI run shows H100 less affected but Ampere and Ampere-midseq saw regression. hypothesis: prefetch logic tuned for fp16/kernel shape on h100
alex: we need criteria for gating. current gating => p99 delta > 10% across allocators. This candidate only tripped ampere. 
maya: propose: add arch-sensitive gating: require that any candidate kernel with p99 delta > 8% on any supported arch fails gate unless rollback patch or opt-out flag
nora: also think we should add seqlen-bucket checks: seq bins [<=128, 129-512, 513-2048, >2048] failing only in >2048 should be treated as high severity if we expect production seq distribution covers it
liam: actionable steps: (1) add reproducer job to nightly with --seq-len=4096 and kv-mode=prefix, (2) revert archwise_v2 from candidate pool for ampere in autotune, (3) instrument KV metrics (evictions, lookups, bandwidth) in harness logs
sam: I'll open follow-up ticket and revert PR temporarily. https://git.internal/r/PR-8142
maya: tag: @eng-runtime @eng-ml
ci-bot: Created job: nightly-repro-3345127890. Artifacts will post to the thread when complete.
liam: also add small microbenchmark: ```microprobe --kernel archwise_v2 --seq 4096 --warm 100 --iter 1000 --trace kv_stats``` for fast regression detection
nora: agreed. after revert, let's run a 72h sweep with varied batch sizes and kv-modes (prefix, cache-only, none) to ensure no stealth regressions
perf-bot: note: autotune logic currently promotes kernels that beat baseline on avg latency across seq mix. We should update scoring to penalize worst-case p99 across seq buckets
maya: thanks team, next steps captured in ticket ENGRT-1609. Assigning to sam + liam. We'll re-run nightly after revert and collect traces.
sam: on it, will post a short digest with repro logs and the reverted patch link.
alex: cc: infra to ensure we have enough ampere capacity for the 72h sweep
ci-bot: Nightly repro finished: artifacts at s3://redwood-ci/archwise_v2/3345127890/repro-run.tar.gz
nora: logs show kv_eviction spikes at iter ~23 consistently. adding a kv cache warmup in harness may mask this — don't do that for the gating test
maya: good catch. keep warm=0 for gating.
liam: plan approved. reverting candidate now and updating autotune scoring. will send patch and notify when rolled out.
maya: :thumbsup:
